d: Low testosterone because the testis itself has failed, as in Klinefelter syndrome, mumps orchitis or chemotherapy. Feedback is lost, so LH and FSH are high. This is also called hypergonadotropic hypogonadism.

Low testosterone because the hypothalamus or pituitary has failed, as in Kallmann syndrome, a pituitary tumor, hyperprolactinemia or opioid use. LH and FSH are low or inappropriately normal. This is also called hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
A hormone made by Sertoli cells under FSH. It feeds back on the pituitary to lower FSH only. A low inhibin B with a high FSH means the seminiferous tubules have failed.

Sex hormone-binding globulin, a liver protein that binds testosterone tightly. It falls in obesity and insulin resistance and rises with aging, thyroid excess and cirrhosis, so total testosterone can mislead. Free testosterone is the active fraction.

Congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens, usually from CFTR mutations. It causes obstructive azoospermia with a low-volume, acidic, fructose-negative ejaculate and normal testes. Both partners need cystic fibrosis carrier testing.
alt: congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens

d: A drug such as sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil or avanafil that blocks the enzyme breaking down cGMP in penile smooth muscle. It strengthens nitric oxide signaling, needs sexual stimulation, and must never be given with nitrates.
A testicular biopsy pattern in which germ cells stop at one stage of spermatogenesis, usually the primary spermatocyte, so no spermatids or sperm form. FSH is normal or high.

Treatment of advanced prostate cancer that lowers testosterone or blocks its receptor, using a GnRH agonist or antagonist, an antiandrogen or abiraterone. Its adverse effects are those of hypogonadism, such as hot flashes, lost libido and bone loss.
